method: A separately specified expected surface list for every defined system is checked against the source proposal and its actual visible table coordinate. Primary grammar pages were directly viewed before certifying the expected forms; the source crosscheck records those views individually.
primary_rule_findings: Cook54§93 assigns strong second-singular preterite to the plural stem; ādrife and fluge therefore do not acquire the first/third-singular long vowel.
Cook58–61 explicitly places flēon in the contracted classII pattern; the contracted present and flīehst/flīehð coexist with flēah/fluge/flugon.
Cook59 makes the contracted classII command long-vowel flēoh, while the inherited slēan command has short-vowel sleah.
Cook67§110 supplies the gehātan-family ē preterite; the ordinary indicative endings and dental present changes supply its twelve selected positions.
Cook68–72 gives the weakI dental patterns, including mētte and ēhte, and the selected gierwed/sętt bases; Cook70 supplies irregular geworht.
Cook24–25 and directly inspected Wright248§476 support selected cȳst/cȳð and checked dental coalescence rather than an arbitrary uniform present suffix.
Cook73–74 supplies the complete weakII present/preterite and command patterns used for geopenian/leornian; the plain and inflected infinitives remain separate precisely bounded systems.
Cook77§127 directly gives āh/āhst/āgon and āhte; twelve indicative positions do not assign its other printed systems.
Every table has a visible lexical caption naming strong, weak, mixed or preterite-present status and the exact system. Recognition participles remain recognition.
The twelve habban clause positions bind existing auxiliaries and are excluded from the152 inflectional cells.
limits: This is a complete coordinate/surface and morphological-rule crosscheck, not a claim that every derived inflection is separately attested on a page. Dictionary sense/argument frames, reading interpretation, all graded solutions, and final rendered pages require their separate audits/review. The reserved solver has not read private models.
